body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「你給 agent 一個 refund_invoice 工具，schema 要求 invoice_id、amount 和 reason，所有欄位都驗證成功。這是否已符合 least privilege？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「欄位有型別、amount 有上限、reason 必填，所以不會亂退款。」

## Schema 和權限在回答不同問題

Tool schema 驗證 request 的形狀：invoice_id 是否存在、amount 是否為數字、reason 是否非空、enum 是否合法。它可以防止 malformed input，也能讓工具呼叫可預測。但 least privilege 問的是另一組問題：這個 actor 可否在此刻、為這個目的、對這張 invoice、在這個金額範圍內做此動作？是否需要 approval？可否只看 preview 而非真正寫入？授權會否過期？下游 service 會否再次獨立驗證？一個欄位完全正確的 request，仍可能由錯誤角色、對錯誤租戶、在錯誤時段或無批准下提出。

模型產生的 tool call 是 untrusted proposal，不是 capability。schema 不應變成把 action authority 交給 prompt 的門票。真正的控制通常在 service side：authenticated principal、resource scope、tenant、role、purpose、action policy、amount limit、approval token、idempotency key 和 audit trail。模型可幫忙提出「想做甚麼」和補充 reason，但它不能自己把 proposal 變成有後果的 write。

## 填好提款表，不等於有提款權

一份填對姓名、日期和金額的提款表格，不能取代銀行卡、身分核對、帳戶權限和每日限額。schema 是表格格式；least privilege 是誰拿著哪張卡、可以從哪個帳戶拿多少、由誰批准。

## 答案在哪裡會變薄

不要為了展示 tool use 就接一個真實 refund API。第一版可以只產生 draft request，或只讓 tool 回傳 mock preview，沒有任何資金、帳戶或外發後果。若要展示一個有寫入形狀的 demo，使用 synthetic ledger 和 sandbox service，並讓所有 non-draft action 必須由 mock reviewer fixture 批准。先證明 deny path、scope check 和 audit receipt，才談 agent autonomy。

## 技術判斷：把 action contract 拆成兩層

第一層是 schema validation：欄位、型別、範圍、格式、與現有資料的基本關聯。第二層是 authorisation decision：principal、tenant、resource ownership、role、purpose、approval state、time window、rate／amount limit 和 policy version。兩層都要在 server side 執行，並輸出可區分的 failure reason：schema_invalid、resource_not_found、scope_denied、approval_missing、approval_expired、limit_exceeded 或 idempotency_conflict。不要把「工具沒有執行」全說成模型輸出不好。

最小測試矩陣至少有：合法 schema 但 wrong role；合法 schema 但 wrong tenant；合法 schema 但 approval 已過期；合法 schema 但金額超限；同一 idempotency key 重送；以及合法 schema、完整 approval 但只允許 preview 的 case。也要測模型用自然語言說「已退款」時，UI 是否只顯示服務端 confirmed receipt，而不是相信模型句子。

## 工程層面：將能力限制放在可撤銷的服務端

給每個 action 最小 scope 的 capability 或 policy decision，而不是給模型一張可做任何事的長期 API key。將 read、preview、draft、approve、execute 分成不同 endpoint 或明確 state；execute 要讀取 server-side approval，不接受模型自填 approved=true。把 request hash、policy version、approval reference、idempotency key、external reference 和 final status 放進 audit event。timeout 或未知結果時，先查詢／對帳，不能以「模型說成功」收尾。

如果工具有第三方整合，將 connector 權限和資料範圍再縮一層，並設明確 revoke path。schema 成功率很高，仍不代表 integration 只在被批准的範圍內操作。

## 交付、業務與風險：誰承受後果要先講

業務 owner 決定可接受的退款、取消、發訊息或資料變更範圍；財務／流程 owner 定義 approval；安全 owner 定義角色和 revoke；support owner 處理被拒絕或不確定結果。監控 schema-pass-but-denied rate、approval expiry、scope violation attempts、preview-to-execute ratio、duplicate action prevention 和 review turnaround。高 deny rate 有時顯示 policy 配置要改善，但不能自動變成「降低 deny rate」的理由。

## 可放進 portfolio 的 artefact

建立 schema-vs-capability-lab：

- schemas/refund-request.json：用作格式驗證，README 明示它不授權 action。
- fixtures/requests.json：完全合成的 invoice、role、tenant、purpose、approval 和 expiry 資料。
- tests/two-layer-authorisation.md：每一行的 schema result、policy result、server receipt 和 expected UI message。
- docs/action-state.md：draft、preview、awaiting_approval、approved、executed、needs_review 的轉換。
- docs/decision-record.md：為何 first release 沒有真實 connector，何種 audit evidence 才可考慮擴大 scope。

## 延伸閱讀

[Agent draft 不作有後果 action](/zh-HK/interview-lab/agent-draft-without-consequential-actions)、[retry 不是 recovery plan](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-retry-is-not-a-recovery-plan) 和 [從需求到驗收](/zh-HK/articles/from-vague-request-to-accepted-feature)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。工具、invoice、approval、ledger 和結果均為虛構或 synthetic sandbox fixture；它不是財務建議、付款功能、任何第三方帳戶連接、已部署權限控制或商業成果聲明。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “You give an agent a refund_invoice tool. Its schema requires invoice_id, amount, and reason, and all fields validate. Does that satisfy least privilege?”
>
> Half-right answer: “The fields have types, amount has a cap, and reason is required, so it cannot issue arbitrary refunds.”

## Schema and authority answer different questions

A tool schema validates a request's shape: whether invoice_id is present, amount is numeric, reason is non-empty, and an enum is allowed. It prevents malformed input and makes calls predictable. Least privilege asks something else: may this actor, at this time, for this purpose, act on this invoice, within this amount range? Is approval required? May it see a preview only rather than write? Has authority expired? Will the downstream service validate independently? A request with every field correct may still come from the wrong role, target the wrong tenant, arrive at the wrong time, or lack approval.

A model-generated tool call is an untrusted proposal, not a capability. A schema must not become a ticket that gives action authority to a prompt. The controls normally live service-side: authenticated principal, resource scope, tenant, role, purpose, action policy, amount limit, approval token, idempotency key, and audit trail. A model can propose an intent and help write a reason. It cannot turn that proposal into a consequential write by itself.

## A filled withdrawal form is not permission

A withdrawal form with the name, date, and amount filled correctly does not replace a bank card, identity check, account rights, and daily limit. The schema is the form format. Least privilege is who holds which card, which account they may use, how much, and who approves it.

## Where an answer goes thin

Do not connect a real refund API just to demonstrate tool use. A first release can produce a draft request only, or return a mock preview with no money, account, or outbound consequence. To show the shape of a write, use a synthetic ledger and sandbox service; require a mock reviewer fixture for every non-draft action. Demonstrate a denial path, scope check, and audit receipt before discussing agent autonomy.

## Technical judgement: split the action contract into two layers

The first layer is schema validation: fields, types, ranges, format, and basic linkage to known data. The second is an authorisation decision: principal, tenant, resource ownership, role, purpose, approval state, time window, rate or amount limit, and policy version. Both execute server-side and return distinguishable reasons: schema_invalid, resource_not_found, scope_denied, approval_missing, approval_expired, limit_exceeded, or idempotency_conflict. Do not describe every non-executed tool call as a model-output failure.

The minimum test matrix includes valid schema with a wrong role, wrong tenant, expired approval, amount above the limit, repeated idempotency key, and a valid fully approved request that is nevertheless preview-only. Test what happens when a model says “the refund is complete” in natural language: the UI must show only a server-confirmed receipt, not trust the sentence.

## Engineering implementation: make capability service-side and revocable

Give each action a minimal-scope capability or policy decision instead of a long-lived API key that can do anything. Separate read, preview, draft, approve, and execute into distinct endpoints or states. Execute reads server-side approval; it does not accept approved=true from a model. Record request hash, policy version, approval reference, idempotency key, external reference, and final status in the audit event. On timeout or unknown outcome, query or reconcile first. “The model said it succeeded” is not a final state.

If a tool connects to a third party, narrow the connector's permissions and data scope again, and provide an explicit revoke path. A high schema-success rate does not prove that an integration acted only within approved scope.

## Delivery, business, and risk

A business owner defines the acceptable scope for refunds, cancellations, outbound messages, or data changes. A finance or process owner defines approval. A security owner defines roles and revocation. A support owner handles denials and uncertain outcomes. Monitor schema-pass-but-denied rate, approval expiry, scope-violation attempts, preview-to-execute ratio, duplicate-action prevention, and review turnaround. A high denial rate may expose a policy configuration problem, but it is not automatically a reason to lower denials.

## A portfolio artefact someone can inspect

Build schema-vs-capability-lab with:

- schemas/refund-request.json: format validation, with a README statement that it does not authorise action.
- fixtures/requests.json: fully synthetic invoice, role, tenant, purpose, approval, and expiry data.
- tests/two-layer-authorisation.md: schema result, policy result, server receipt, and expected UI message for each row.
- docs/action-state.md: draft, preview, awaiting_approval, approved, executed, and needs_review transitions.
- docs/decision-record.md: why the first release has no real connector and what audit evidence would justify wider scope.

## Further reading

[Agent drafts without consequential actions](/en/interview-lab/agent-draft-without-consequential-actions), [a retry is not a recovery plan](/en/interview-lab/a-retry-is-not-a-recovery-plan), and [move from a vague request to an accepted feature](/en/articles/from-vague-request-to-accepted-feature).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. Its tools, invoices, approvals, ledger, and results are fictional or synthetic sandbox fixtures. It is not financial advice, a payment feature, a third-party account connection, deployed access control, or a business-outcome claim.
